blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Monetary policy is the process by which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) controls the supply of money and interest rates.
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members: 3 from the RBI and 3 appointed by the Central Government.
Key monetary policy instruments are categorized into quantitative (Repo Rate, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR) and qualitative tools.
Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) is used by RBI to manage day-to-day liquidity in the banking system.
India follows a Flexible Inflation Targeting Framework with Consumer Price Index (CPI) as the primary anchor.

blocks.content: Monetary Policy refers to the actions taken by RBI to control money supply and interest rates to achieve macroeconomic goals such as controlling inflation, fostering growth, maintaining exchange rate stability, and ensuring financial stability.
The MPC was constituted under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934 (amended 2016). It has 6 members: 3 from RBI (including the Governor who chairs it) and 3 external members appointed by the Government.
Note: MPC meets at least 4 times a year. Decisions taken by majority vote; Governor has casting vote in case of a tie.

blocks.content: Note: CRR and SLR are quantitative tools. Repo, Reverse Repo, Bank Rate are qualitative tools. Both affect credit availability.

LAF is an RBI tool to manage day-to-day liquidity in the banking system. It operates through overnight Repo (injection) and Reverse Repo (abGBOrption) auctions. Banks can borrow overnight against G-secs.

items: MPC Composition: 6 members; the RBI Governor holds the casting vote in case of a tie.
Flexible Inflation Target: 4% CPI inflation with a band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%).
CRR vs SLR: CRR is held in cash with RBI, while SLR is held by banks themselves in liquid assets like G-Secs.

blocks.content: India adopted Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) in 2016. The target is CPI inflation of 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (i.e., 2%–6%). If inflation stays above/below target for 3 consecutive quarters, RBI must explain and submit remedial plan to Govt.
